avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer reduces budesonide bioavailability and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative herbal products

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice Root (high dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive mineralocorticoid effects increase hypertension and hypokalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under medical supervision with electrolyte monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase budesonide levels; effect typically modest with enteric formulation
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased steroid side effects; separate dosing if possible

caution_supplements.name: Calcium and Vitamin D supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Long-term corticosteroids impair calcium absorption; supplementation recommended
caution_supplements.action: Ensure adequate intake (1000-1200 mg calcium, 800-2000 IU vitamin D daily)

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases systemic budesonide exposure and adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Avoid consumption; choose alternative citrus fruits

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Corticosteroids promote sodium retention and fluid accumulation
caution_foods.action: Moderate sodium intake; monitor blood pressure and fluid status

caution_foods.name: Foods high in potassium-depleting diuretics
caution_foods.mechanism: Budesonide may cause hypokalemia; adequate dietary potassium intake important
caution_foods.action: Maintain adequate potassium through diet (bananas, leafy greens, legumes)

monitoring_notes: Monitor blood pressure, electrolytes (especially potassium), and bone density with long-term use. Assess for signs of adrenal suppression and GI irritation, particularly in patients with IBD.
